intro: Degrees of friendship, love affairs, and the celebrations where everyone meets.
p.íntimo.consejo: You say «un amigo íntimo». The accent falls on the first «í»: «IN-ti-mo».
p.de toda la vida.consejo: It goes after the noun: «amigos de toda la vida». It does not change with gender.
p.conocer de vista.consejo: It is «conocer» + «de vista»: «lo conozco de vista». You do not talk.
p.conocido.consejo: It sits between «desconocido» and «amigo». It is also the participle of «conocer».
p.ligar.consejo: It is colloquial. The noun is «el ligue»: «tiene un ligue».
p.romper con.consejo: It takes «con» and the person: «rompí con mi novio». «Romper algo» is breaking it.
p.invitado.consejo: It comes from «invitar». «Los invitados» arrive and the anfitrión welcomes them.
p.anfitrión.consejo: The feminine is «anfitriona» and loses the accent.
p.bodas de plata.consejo: Always plural. At fifty years they are «bodas de oro».
p.banquete.consejo: It sounds «ban-KE-te»: «qu» is a «k». There are wedding banquets.
p.discurso.consejo: You «give» or «pronounce» a speech. A short one is «unas palabras».
p.brindar.consejo: You toast «por» something or someone: «brindamos por los novios».
p.asistir a.consejo: False friend: «asistir a» is being present. To help is «ayudar».
p.caer bien.consejo: It works like «gustar»: «me cae bien tu hermano». It is not attraction.
b1.titulo: How well do you know them?
b1.texto:
**Degrees.** **Lo conozco de vista.** **Es un conocido.** **Es un compañero.** **Es un amigo íntimo.** **Es un amigo de toda la vida.**

**Liking or disliking.** With a person, «gustar» suggests attraction. Use **caer**: **me cae bien**, **me cae fatal**, **me cayó genial**.

**Love.** **Ligar**, **un ligue**, **salir con** someone, **tener un compromiso**, **romper con** someone.

**Celebrations.** **Una boda**, **un aniversario**, **un cumpleaños**. Twenty-five years of marriage are **las bodas de plata**; fifty, **las bodas de oro**.

**What happens at a party.** **El anfitrión** welcomes **los invitados**. There is **una ceremonia** and then **un banquete**. Someone gives **un discurso** or **dice unas palabras**, everyone **brinda** and the presents are **envueltos**.

**Verbs for events.** **Celebrar**, **organizar**, **cancelar**, **asistir a**. Careful: **asistir a una boda** is being present; to help is **ayudar**.
b2.f0.texto: Tomorrow we attend Blanca and Rodrigo's silver wedding.
b2.f2.texto: I only know the husband by sight.
b2.f3.texto: Well, you will meet lots of people you will like.
b2.f4.texto: After the ceremony there will be an enormous banquet.
b2.f6.texto: The eldest son will give it; he is very funny.
b2.f7.texto: At the end we will drink a toast to the hosts.
b4.titulo: Caer bien and verbs with a fixed preposition
b4.texto:
**Caer bien or mal.** The person who is liked is the subject; whoever has the opinion goes in **me, te, le, nos, os, les**: **me cae bien tu hermano**, **me caen bien tus amigos**, **me cayó fatal**.

**Verbs with a fixed preposition.** Each verb asks for its own:

- **asistir a**: asistí **a** la boda
- **brindar por**: brindamos **por** los novios
- **romper con**: rompió **con** su novio
- **salir con**: sale **con** una compañera
b4.e0.texto: I like your brother a lot.
b4.e2.texto: She broke up with her boyfriend after two years.
b5.f0.texto: On Saturday I attended the silver wedding of some lifelong friends.
b5.f1.texto: There were almost a hundred guests under a marquee full of lights.
b5.f2.texto: The hostess welcomed each person with a long hug and a smile.
b5.f3.texto: Among the guests there were dear faces and others I only knew by sight.
b5.f4.texto: On the tables the candles drew small golden circles on the tablecloths.
b5.f5.texto: After a simple ceremony came a banquet that lasted until night.
b5.f6.texto: The eldest son gave a short speech, with his voice trembling with emotion.
b5.f7.texto: When he finished, everyone raised their glasses and drank a toast to the hosts.
b5.f8.texto: They sat me next to a cousin of Rodrigo's whom I could not stand at first.
b5.f9.texto: In the end we finished up dancing together until the lights went out.
b6.o0.refuerzo: Yes: you know who he is, but you do not talk to him.
b6.o1.refuerzo: A close friend is someone very near to you.
b6.o2: Es un amigo de toda la vida
b6.o2.refuerzo: That is a lot of trust; here you have only seen him.
b6.pregunta: How do you know someone you have only seen?
b7.o0.refuerzo: Yes: «caer bien» says you like him as a person.
b7.o1.refuerzo: With a person, «gustar» sounds like attraction.
b7.o2.refuerzo: «Querer» is feeling affection; here you need «caer».
b7.pregunta: Which verb avoids sounding like attraction?
b8.frase: Brindamos por los anfitriones de la fiesta
b8.traduccion: We drank a toast to the hosts of the party
b9.o1.refuerzo: To help is «ayudar»; asistir is being present.
b9.o2.refuerzo: It looks similar, but «insistí» is another word.
b10.frase: Veinticinco años de matrimonio son las bodas de ____.
b10.o0.refuerzo: The golden wedding is at fifty years.
b10.o1.refuerzo: Yes: twenty-five years are the silver wedding.
b10.o2.refuerzo: The diamond wedding is at sixty years.
b10.pregunta: Choose the metal for twenty-five years.
b12.o0.refuerzo: Yes: «romper con» is ending a relationship.
b12.o1: Rompió un objeto de su novio
b12.o1.refuerzo: For that it would be «rompió algo», without «con».
b12.o2: Se fue de viaje con él
p.asistimos.consejo: «Asistir a» an event is being present at it. This is the «nosotros» form.
p.vista.consejo: In «conocer de vista» it is not the sense of sight: you only know who the person is.
p.caerá.consejo: Future of «caer». The accent marks the last syllable. «Te caerá bien» means you will like him as a person.
p.ceremonia.consejo: The «c» sounds «th» and «io» forms a diphthong: «the-re-MO-nya».
p.dará.consejo: Future of «dar»: the accent marks the last syllable. «Dar un discurso» is giving a speech.
p.gracioso.consejo: The feminine is «graciosa». It comes from «gracia». The «c» sounds «th».
p.brindaremos.consejo: Future for «nosotros» of «brindar». You toast «por» something: «brindaremos por los novios».
p.anfitriones.consejo: Plural of «anfitrión»; it loses the accent: «anfitriones».
p.asistí.consejo: Past for «yo»: the accent marks the last syllable. It still goes with «a»: «asistí a la boda».
p.rompió.consejo: The accent marks the last syllable. The participle of «romper» is irregular: «roto».
p.novio.consejo: The feminine is «novia». At a wedding, «los novios» are the couple getting married.
p.invitados.consejo: Plural of «invitado»; it comes from «invitar». The «v» sounds «b».
p.carpa.consejo: It is a big tent for parties. It is also a fish: «la carpa».
p.anfitriona.consejo: It is the feminine of «anfitrión» and has no accent.
p.recibía.consejo: The accented «í» breaks the diphthong: «rre-thi-BÍ-a». It is the imperfect of «recibir».
p.caras.consejo: Plural of «cara». «Caras queridas» are people you love.
p.otras.consejo: Feminine plural of «otro». Here it stands for the noun: «otras» means other faces.
p.conocía.consejo: Imperfect of «conocer»: the accent marks the «í». The «c» sounds «th».
p.dorados.consejo: From «oro», gold. The plural «dorados» agrees with «círculos», so it ends in -os.
p.manteles.consejo: Think of «mantel» as the cloth that covers a table. The plural «manteles» is masculine.
p.duró.consejo: From «durar», to last. The accent on «ó» marks the past tense, like «habló».
p.temblorosa.consejo: From «temblor», a tremble. It describes the voice, so it ends in -a: «la voz temblorosa».
p.emoción.consejo: The accent on the «ó» is needed because the word ends in -n and is stressed on the last syllable.
p.levantaron.consejo: From «levantar», to raise. The ending -aron is the ustedes/ellos past tense of -ar verbs.
p.brindaron.consejo: From «brindar», to make a toast. Same ending as «levantaron»: -aron, for ellos in the past.
p.sentaron.consejo: From «sentar», to seat. Here «me sentaron» means they sat me down, with «me» as the person seated.
p.primo.consejo: Careful: «primo» is a cousin, not a «first». Its feminine form is «prima».
p.cayó.consejo: From «caer», to fall. «Me cayó fatal» means I took an instant dislike to him.
p.acabamos.consejo: From «acabar», to finish. «Acabar» plus a gerund means ending up doing something.
p.bailando.consejo: From «bailar», to dance. The -ando ending is the gerund, the -ing form in English.
p.apagaron.consejo: From «apagar», to switch off. The opposite is «encender», to switch on.
p.brindamos.consejo: From «brindar», to make a toast. The ending -amos means «we». The d is soft.
p.matrimonio.consejo: The ñ sound is written «ny». In «matrimonio» the stress falls on the «mo» syllable.
p.bodas.consejo: «Boda» is a wedding. The plural «bodas» is used for anniversaries, like «bodas de plata».
p.terminó.consejo: From «terminar», to end. The accent on the «ó» shows the past tense of él.
